meta.purpose: Prioritized source of truth for the build. Every challenge requirement maps to a feature here. Work strictly top-down by tier.
howToUse: Pick the next feature with status 'failing' in the lowest-numbered tier.
Implement the thinnest vertical slice that satisfies its acceptance criteria.
Make its listed tests pass and run `pnpm verify` (must exit 0).
Flip status to 'passing' and commit in the same change.
Do NOT begin any Tier 1 feature until every Tier 0 feature is 'passing'.

statusLegend.failing: Target not yet met (not implemented, or acceptance criteria/tests not satisfied). Initial state for everything.
statusLegend.passing: Acceptance criteria met, tests green, no invariant violated.
statusLegend.blocked: Cannot proceed until a dependency is resolved.

tiers.0: AIRTIGHT CORE + INFRASTRUCTURE. Must be perfect. These are what the challenge says must be airtight; they are graded hardest.
tiers.1: CORE DIFFERENTIATORS. Build only after every Tier 0 item is passing.
tiers.2: PIONEER / STRETCH. Only if Tier 0 + Tier 1 are solid. One or two well-chosen items here make you stand out.

meta.invariantsRef: See AGENTS.md §2 — no feature may violate a non-negotiable invariant.

features.title: Secrets via AWS Secrets Manager / Parameter Store
features.description: All DB credentials and API keys load at runtime from AWS Secrets Manager or Parameter Store. Nothing sensitive is committed.
acceptance: No credential, API key, or token appears anywhere in the repo, including committed .env files.
.env is git-ignored; .env.example documents shape with placeholders only.
The running app reads real secrets from Secrets Manager via an EC2 IAM role (no keys on disk).

features.title: RDS Postgres (private, pgvector) as the only durable store
features.description: Provision RDS PostgreSQL in a private subnet with pgvector enabled. It is the sole persistence layer.
acceptance: RDS has no public IP; security group accepts 5432 only from the EC2 security group.
pgvector extension is enabled for ICD-10 similarity search.
No SQLite, in-memory, or flat-file persistence exists anywhere for durable data.
Public connection attempts to RDS are refused (demonstrable in the walkthrough).
features.rubric: Infrastructure rigor: VPC isolation of RDS

features.title: Correct DB connection pooling
features.description: A single bounded connection pool per process. The instance never opens a new DB connection per request.
acceptance: One shared pool is created at startup and reused across requests.
Pool size is bounded and configurable; documented awareness of RDS max_connections (RDS Proxy/PgBouncer for scale).
A load test shows connection count stays bounded, not one-per-request.

features.title: EC2 behind nginx with valid HTTPS
features.description: App hosted on EC2, reachable over HTTPS with a valid (non-self-signed) certificate, behind an nginx reverse proxy.
acceptance: nginx terminates TLS on 443 and proxies to the Node process on localhost.
The Node process is NOT directly exposed on port 80 or 443.
Certificate is valid and CA-issued (e.g. Let's Encrypt), not self-signed.

features.title: Normalized schema + migrations + defensible ERD
features.description: A normalized relational schema managed by migrations, with an ERD you can defend table-by-table.
acceptance: Tables: providers, patients, encounters, note_versions, templates, audit_logs, drafts, icd10_codes (with vector column).
All FKs, patient-match columns, and the vector column are indexed appropriately (HNSW/IVFFlat for vectors).
Schema is created and evolved exclusively through migrations.
An ERD diagram exists and every table/relationship can be justified.
features.rubric: Database design: schema quality, normalization, indexing

features.title: Real login with JWT/session tokens
features.description: A working login system issuing JWTs or session tokens, with hashed passwords and token expiry.
acceptance: Passwords hashed with argon2/bcrypt; never stored or logged in plaintext.
Tokens carry role + identity and have an expiry.
Every layer (issuance, storage, guard, expiry) is explainable in the walkthrough.

features.title: Provider + Admin roles with seeded demo accounts
features.description: Two distinct roles. Seed at least three provider accounts and one admin account (hashed passwords) for the demo.
acceptance: Roles: provider and admin, enforced by guards.
Seed script creates >=3 providers and 1 admin with hashed passwords.
Role determines access to provider vs admin surfaces.

features.title: Provider data isolation
features.description: Providers can see and act on only their own encounters. Admin-wide access only via an explicit admin guard.
acceptance: Every provider-facing query is scoped to the authenticated provider_id.
Provider A requesting Provider B's encounter receives 403.
Admin can access all encounters through an admin-only guard.

features.title: Start a new encounter
features.description: A logged-in provider starts an encounter by entering patient first name, last name, and date of birth.
acceptance: Encounter is created and linked to the authenticated provider and a patient record.
Patient identity is first name + last name + DOB.
Encounter persists to RDS with a draft status.

features.title: Transcript / freeform input
features.description: The provider pastes a raw encounter transcript or types freeform clinical observations into a text area.
acceptance: A text area accepts pasted transcript or freeform notes.
Input is associated with the open encounter.
The workspace looks like a clinical tool (clean, dense, high-trust).

features.title: Generate SOAP note with SSE streaming
features.description: Clicking Generate Note streams a structured SOAP note back in real time via server-sent events, rendering progressively.
acceptance: Generation streams token-by-token via SSE; the UI renders progressively.
No full-page reload and no spinner-then-dump.
A test confirms multiple chunks arrive over time, not a single blob.

features.title: Structured S/O/A/P output
features.description: The generated note includes Subjective, Objective, Assessment, and Plan sections.
acceptance: All four SOAP sections are present and clearly delineated.
Sections are populated from the clinical input, not boilerplate.

features.title: ICD-10 code(s) in the Assessment
features.description: The Assessment includes at least one suggested ICD-10 code and description semantically matched to the clinical content.
acceptance: >=1 ICD-10 code + description appears in the Assessment.
The code is semantically relevant to the input, not random.
No fabricated codes — codes come from the embedded ICD-10 set.

features.title: Inline edit before save
features.description: The provider can edit the generated note inline before saving (human-in-the-loop).
acceptance: All sections are editable in place.
Edits are preserved through to save.

features.title: Save finalized note to RDS
features.description: The finalized note is saved to RDS.
acceptance: Saving writes the note to RDS (never memory or a file).
The saved note is retrievable and tied to the encounter and provider.

features.title: Immutable note versioning
features.description: Every edit-and-re-save writes a new version to RDS. Prior versions are never overwritten or deleted.
acceptance: Re-saving INSERTs a new note_versions row; no UPDATE/DELETE of existing versions.
Editing a note twice leaves version 1 byte-for-byte unchanged and retrievable.
Each version records who saved it and when.

features.title: View full version history
features.description: Providers can view the full version history of any note, including author and timestamp per version, retrieved from RDS.
acceptance: Version history lists every version with author + timestamp.
History is read from RDS, not memory or a file.

features.title: Admin route + role-gated shell
features.fixPrompt: Add AdminRoute + AdminShell: role-gated /admin route as the frontend attachment point for the backend admin surface (already guarded by RolesGuard). A provider hitting /admin must be blocked/redirected, enforced by both API guard and frontend route gate.
features.description: A dedicated /admin area exists, reachable only by the admin role, with a nav shell that the rest of the admin features (view-all, roster, templates) attach their pages to. This is the concrete first step behind ‘we don’t have an admin route to list all’ — added as its own small feature so it's independently buildable and testable, rather than bundled inside admin.view_all.
acceptance: An /admin route exists and renders a distinct admin shell (nav/layout), separate from the provider workspace.
Only the admin role can reach it — a provider hitting /admin is redirected or blocked (403), enforced by both the API guard and the frontend route gate.
The shell is the single attachment point the rest of the admin features (view-all, roster, templates) render into.

features.title: Admin: view all encounters (filterable)
features.fixPrompt: Add admin DTOs (roster + encounter filter) in shared-types. Add GET /admin/encounters (filterable by providerId/from/to) behind AdminController's existing class-level @Roles('admin') guard.
features.description: Admins view all encounters across providers, filterable by provider and date range.
acceptance: Admin-only view lists all encounters across providers.
Filters by provider and by date range work.
Non-admins cannot reach this view.

features.title: Admin: manage provider roster
features.fixPrompt: Add GET/POST /admin/providers and PATCH /admin/providers/:id/deactivate behind AdminController's admin guard. Provider creation hashes via AuthService.hashPassword; ProviderSummary DTO structurally excludes password. Define deactivation behavior: only flips is_active, never touches provider data, session ends on their next authenticated request (JwtStrategy re-checks is_active per request), not immediately — add a test proving an already-issued unexpired JWT gets 401'd on the next call after deactivation.
features.description: Admins can add and deactivate provider accounts.
acceptance: Admin can create a new provider account.
Admin can deactivate a provider; deactivated providers cannot log in.
Deactivation behavior for an open draft is defined (see edge.provider_deactivated).

features.title: Admin: template library CRUD
features.fixPrompt: Require @Roles('admin') on POST/PATCH/DELETE /templates; leave GET open to any authenticated provider. Same controller, RolesGuard already handles per-method — no separate admin controller needed.
features.description: Admins create, edit, and delete note templates (structured prompts that shape generation for different encounter types).
acceptance: Admin can create, edit, and delete templates.
Templates persist in RDS.

features.title: Provider selects template; AI behaves differently
features.fixPrompt: Add template-apply.e2e-spec.ts: prove an identical transcript under two different templates produces genuinely different Plan text carrying each template's own name/instructions, no template selected produces plain output, and a client-supplied templateApplied payload on the generate request is structurally ignored (ScribeController has no @Body() param to carry it).
features.description: Providers select a template before generating; the AI visibly behaves differently depending on the active template.
acceptance: Provider can pick a template before Generate Note.
Output visibly differs by template (e.g. ortho follow-up vs new-patient eval).
The template is applied server-side, not from the client prompt.

features.title: Live template updates (no refresh)
features.fixPrompt: Add template-live-update.e2e-spec.ts: prove an admin edit to a template's promptInstructions takes effect on the same open encounter's very next generation, no new encounter and no page refresh needed (TemplatesRepository.findById has no caching layer), plus a regression guard that a note saved before the edit keeps its original plan text forever (VERSION-IMMUTABILITY).
features.description: If an admin updates the active template while a provider has the workspace open, the provider's next generation uses the new template without a page refresh.
acceptance: Admin edits a template; the provider's next generation uses the new version.
No page refresh is required for the change to take effect.
features.rubric: Admin dashboard: templates take effect immediately

features.title: Admin: wire shell nav to real pages
features.description: The /admin shell's nav (Encounters, Roster, Templates, Audit Log) currently renders as static <li> text with no routes behind it — clicking any item does nothing. Backend endpoints for all four sections already exist (GET /admin/encounters, GET/POST /admin/providers + deactivate, templates CRUD, GET /admin/audit-logs) but nothing in the frontend calls them. Wire each nav item to a real nested route + page that calls the existing API and renders real data.
acceptance: Each of the four nav items is a real link (e.g. NavLink) to a nested route under /admin, not inert text.
/admin index redirects to /admin/encounters; AdminRoute's admin-only gate still covers every nested route.
Encounters page lists all encounters via GET /admin/encounters and supports provider + date-range filters.
Roster page lists providers via GET /admin/providers, can create a provider (POST) and deactivate one (PATCH .../deactivate).
Templates page lists templates and supports create/edit/delete via the templates CRUD endpoints.
Audit Log page lists entries via GET /admin/audit-logs, filterable by actor/action/date-range.
No nav item leads to a dead/placeholder page — each renders real data from its backend endpoint.
features.rubric: Admin dashboard: nav must lead to working pages, not placeholders
features.fixPrompt: Wire the /admin shell nav (Encounters/Roster/Templates/Audit Log) to real nested routes + pages calling the existing backend endpoints (GET /admin/encounters, GET/POST /admin/providers + deactivate, templates CRUD, GET /admin/audit-logs). /admin index redirects to /admin/encounters, AdminRoute's guard still covers every nested route. No nav item may lead to a dead/placeholder page.

features.title: Professional design pass across provider + admin UI
features.description: A live walkthrough (2026-08-18) of login, encounter list, encounter workspace (incl. a generated note), and all 4 admin pages found the UI does not read as a high-trust clinical tool, violating AGENTS.md §1's 'clean, dense, professional' requirement. Concrete findings: (1) SAFETY GAP — the encounter workspace shows no patient name/DOB anywhere, so a provider with multiple tabs open cannot confirm whose chart they're editing; (2) one accent blue is used for every button with no semantic distinction — 'Delete'/'Deactivate' look identical to 'Save'/'Create', no danger styling on destructive actions despite --danger tokens already existing in styles.css (only used for error text); (3) SOAP note sections are fixed-height monospace <textarea>s that clip content behind an internal scrollbar — reads like a code editor, not a clinical note; (4) no brand mark anywhere, just a text wordmark; (5) encounter-list/version-history row hover inverts the whole row to solid navy — heavy-handed for a dense clinical list; (6) almost no type scale — 14px body nearly everywhere; (7) native <select>/<input type=date> look visually inconsistent with the custom-styled text inputs/buttons around them; (8) workspace's 3-column panel grid has ragged, misaligned panel bottoms. Scope covers BOTH the provider workspace and the admin shell (user confirmed 'everything' when asked). Direction: Claude proposes the design system (user confirmed, no external reference given) — keep the existing neutral ink/canvas palette but formalize a real type scale and semantic button variants (primary/secondary/danger), add a persistent patient-identity header to the workspace, and a small brand mark in both shells. SOAP note editor: auto-growing sections in a normal readable font, replacing the fixed-height monospace textareas (user confirmed this interaction change).
acceptance: Encounter workspace shows a persistent patient identity header (first + last name, DOB) so the open chart is unambiguous at a glance — the safety-relevant gap, non-negotiable.

A defined button system with primary/secondary/danger variants is applied consistently everywhere: Save/Create/Generate/Add = primary, Edit/Cancel = secondary, Delete/Deactivate = danger. No destructive action shares styling with a constructive one.
SOAP note sections (Subjective/Objective/Assessment/Plan) auto-grow to their content in a normal (non-monospace) readable font — no fixed-height internal scrollbar.

A defined type scale (distinct, consistent sizes/weights for page title / section header / label / body) replaces the near-uniform 14px treatment, applied across both the provider workspace and admin shell.
A small brand mark (icon/logo, not just a text wordmark) appears in both the provider header and the admin header.
List/table row hover states use a subtle highlight (e.g. tinted background + accent border), not a full solid-color inversion — covers the encounter list, version history list, and admin tables.
Native form controls (select, date input) are visually consistent with text inputs (border, radius, height, focus ring) in both the workspace and admin filters/forms.
The workspace's 3-column panel grid has consistent, non-ragged panel bottoms at common viewport widths.
No regression: `pnpm verify` stays green; existing component tests updated for any changed markup, unchanged in intent.
tests: Manual: live browser walkthrough of login / encounter list / workspace (incl. a generated note) / all 4 admin pages, screenshotted before and after
features.rubric: UI quality: professional, high-trust clinical tool feel (AGENTS.md §1)
features.fixPrompt: Do the professional design pass: add a real type scale, btn-secondary/btn-danger button variants, a small BrandMark icon, AutoGrowTextarea for SOAP sections (replacing fixed-height monospace textareas), subtle (not full-invert) row hover, styled select/date controls, stretch-aligned workspace grid. Add a persistent patient-identity header to the encounter workspace — GET /encounters/:id must return patient {firstName,lastName,dob}. Fix encounters.mapper.ts to normalize patient.dob the same way pdf-export.service.ts already does (pg returns date columns as a JS Date at runtime despite the type saying string, which rendered 'Invalid Date').

features.title: Draft persistence across refresh
features.fixPrompt: Add draft DTOs (SaveDraftRequest, DraftResponse) in shared-types. Add backend PUT/GET /encounters/:id/draft upserting a single row per encounter (drafts table's UNIQUE(encounter_id), already existed unused since Tier 0), tenant-gated through the same EncountersService.getForUser check as every other encounter-scoped route. NotesService.save() deletes the draft row after a real save, strictly after the note_versions INSERT. Frontend: EncounterWorkspacePage fetches the draft on mount and debounce-saves on every note change, guarded by the generating flag so no draft write fires mid-SSE-stream.
features.description: A mid-encounter draft (transcript entered, note not yet saved) is restored from the database after a refresh or browser close/reopen.
acceptance: In-progress draft state is written to RDS as it changes.
After refresh or close/reopen, the provider resumes exactly where they left off.

features.title: Cross-device draft restore
features.fixPrompt: Add draft-cross-device.e2e-spec.ts: two independent logins for the same provider (zero shared client state) see the identical draft, and an edit from one is visible from the other on next fetch — proves draft state is keyed to provider+encounter in RDS, not the browser (backend already added by session.draft_persist).
features.description: Logging in from a different browser/device restores the same in-progress draft state.
acceptance: Draft state is keyed to the provider + encounter in RDS, not to the browser.
A different browser/device shows the same restored draft.

features.title: Non-happy-path: no clinical content
features.fixPrompt: Add edge-no-content.e2e-spec.ts hitting the real POST /scribe/generate route with empty/garbage transcript: assert the stream contains only an insufficient_content frame (no token/done frames), encounter status stays 'draft', and no note_versions row is written. Complements the existing hasClinicalContent() unit test with live HTTP coverage.
features.description: A transcript with no clinically meaningful content is handled gracefully — the AI does not fabricate a SOAP note.
acceptance: Empty/garbage clinical input returns a clear 'insufficient content' response.
No hallucinated SOAP note or ICD-10 code is generated.
Demonstrated explicitly in the walkthrough.

features.title: Non-happy-path: save with expired session
features.fixPrompt: Add edge-expired-save.e2e-spec.ts: a save attempt with an invalid/expired token fails cleanly (401), writes zero note_versions rows, and never touches the already-persisted draft; a fresh login retrieves the identical draft and completes the save. Real 8h JWT expiry isn't waitable in a test — an invalid token exercises the same JwtStrategy rejection path.
features.description: A provider attempting to save while their session has expired is handled without data loss.
acceptance: An expired-session save does not lose the provider's work.
The provider is re-authenticated (or the draft is preserved) and can complete the save.
Demonstrated explicitly in the walkthrough.

features.title: Audit log of saves and admin actions
features.fixPrompt: Add AuditLog/AuditLogFilter DTOs in shared-types. Wire the existing AuditService.log()/listAll() (previously only called from NotesService.save()) into the admin write paths that don't call it yet: AdminService.createProvider/deactivateProvider, TemplatesController create/update/delete — metadata scoped to structural facts only (email, role, version number, changed field names), never a password or clinical content. Expose listAll() via GET /admin/audit-logs (admin-only, same @Roles('admin') gate), filterable by actor/action/date-range, joining providers for actor name. Evaluator-required fix: add the missing date-range filter test.
features.description: Audit logs capture who did what and when for note saves and admin actions, stored in RDS.
acceptance: Note saves and admin actions (roster/template changes) write audit rows with actor, action, target, timestamp.
Audit logs live in RDS and are queryable.

features.title: Pioneer: version diff view
features.fixPrompt: Add a frontend-only version diff view: hand-rolled LCS line-diff (no external dependency) rendered per SOAP section plus a set-diff on icd10Codes, with two compare dropdowns in EncounterWorkspacePage that render the diff panel once both versions are selected. Reuses note.version_history's existing endpoint — no backend change needed.
features.description: A diff view between note versions so providers can see exactly what changed. Cheap to add given immutable versions already exist.
acceptance: Provider can select two versions and see a highlighted diff.
Diff is accurate at the section/line level.

features.title: Pioneer: provider writing-style learning
features.fixPrompt: Add deterministic provider writing-style learning: scan a provider's own recently saved notes for a real, repeated 'pt' vs 'patient' abbreviation preference and apply it to their next generated note. No LLM call, no adaptation without a clear repeated pattern, byte-identical default output otherwise.
features.description: The AI adapts to how a specific provider tends to phrase their notes over time, based on their history in the database.
acceptance: Generation reflects a provider's prior phrasing patterns drawn from their saved notes.
The adaptation is server-side and demonstrable across a provider's history.

features.title: Pioneer: clinical red-flag flagging
features.fixPrompt: Add a deterministic regex-based clinical red-flag detector (no LLM call, tenant-scoped endpoint) plus a frontend advisory banner that fetches on mount and after each debounced transcript save (awaited, so the scan can't race the save); generate button stays enabled regardless of flags. Evaluator-required fixes: match 'difficulty breathing' as a literal phrase, and detect plural seizure/convulsion forms.
features.description: Automatically flag clinical red flags in the transcript before note generation.
acceptance: Red-flag terms/patterns are surfaced to the provider before generation.
Flags are advisory (human-in-the-loop), not blocking.

features.title: Pioneer: bulk patient PDF export
features.fixPrompt: Add GET /patients/:id/export: bulk PDF export of a patient's full encounter history via pdfkit, tenant-scoped (provider sees own encounters only, admin sees all), audit-logged, no fabricated content for encounters without a saved note. Evaluator-required fixes: sanitize the exported filename (was crashing for non-Latin-1 patient names), and document audit-at-generation-success rather than chasing an unachievable delivery-confirmation guarantee.
features.description: Bulk export of all encounters for a given patient across all visits as a single structured PDF.
acceptance: A patient's encounters export to one structured, readable PDF.
Export respects tenant isolation and audit logging.

features.title: Match returning patients
features.fixPrompt: Add patient-match.e2e-spec.ts proving same first+last+dob links to one patient record across encounters and across providers; different DOB or name never merges. The matching behavior already existed via PatientsRepository dedup from Tier 0 — this adds the dedicated e2e coverage feature-list.json requires.
features.description: Detect when an encounter is for a patient who already has saved notes, matched by first name, last name, and DOB.
acceptance: Starting an encounter for an existing patient (first+last+DOB) links to that patient.
First-time patients create a new patient record.

features.title: Backend tool-call history injection
features.fixPrompt: Add context-injection.e2e-spec.ts proving POST .../scribe/generate takes no request body capable of carrying prior history (ScribeController has no @Body() param) via an adversarial fabricated body with zero effect on output, and that cross-provider history sharing works for a shared patient while direct encounter access still 403s. Behavior already existed via Tier 0's ScribeService patientHistoryTool. Required first clarifying AGENTS.md's TENANT-ISOLATION wording (human sign-off 2026-08-17) to settle that it governs direct access to another provider's encounter record, not a patient's clinical history, which may cross providers treating the same patient.
features.description: For a returning patient, the AI retrieves and injects prior encounter history as context during generation via a backend tool/function call — not by stuffing prior notes into the frontend prompt.
acceptance: Prior history is fetched by a backend tool/function call during generation.
Prior notes are never sent from or through the frontend prompt.
The AI references relevant prior diagnoses/treatments where clinically appropriate.

features.title: Returning vs first-time behavior differs
features.fixPrompt: Add context-behavior.e2e-spec.ts proving a returning patient's generated Plan demonstrably references the prior visit's date and plan text while a first-time patient's does not, traced into libs/ai/mock-provider.ts to confirm the assertion is structurally tied to the tool-call result, not coincidental text overlap.
features.description: Generation demonstrably behaves differently for a returning patient versus a first-time patient.
acceptance: A returning patient's note reflects injected history; a first-time patient's does not.
The difference is demonstrable in the walkthrough.

features.title: pgvector ICD-10 semantic search
features.fixPrompt: Add dedicated e2e coverage (icd10-search.e2e-spec.ts) for the already-working GET /icd10/search: relevance, limit-param, empty-query-rejection, and auth-required, against the real 234-code seeded set.
features.description: Semantic search over an embedded subset (200-300+) of ICD-10 codes using pgvector cosine similarity. No external ICD-10 API.
acceptance: 200-300+ ICD-10 codes are embedded and stored in a pgvector column in RDS.
A plain-English query returns the top semantically relevant codes.
No external ICD-10 API is used.

features.title: ICD-10 search widget
features.fixPrompt: Add Icd10SearchWidget.tsx: standalone plain-English search, ranked results, per-result Add button (disabled/labeled 'Added' once a code is already on the note), injectable search prop defaulting to the real icd10Api.search client. Evaluator-required fix: add icd10.test.ts asserting the widget's real wiring to icd10Api.search (URL/query-encoding, default limit, error propagation) — existing tests only injected a mocked search prop. Along the way, fix Node 25's native localStorage shadowing jsdom's in vitest via a minimal in-memory Storage polyfill in apps/web/src/test/setup.ts.
features.description: A standalone ICD-10 search widget in the encounter workspace where a provider types a symptom/condition in plain English.
acceptance: The widget accepts plain-English input and shows ranked results.
Results show code + description.

features.title: Append ICD-10 result to Assessment
features.fixPrompt: Wire Icd10SearchWidget's onAppendIcd10 to add {code, description} to the note's icd10Codes with client-side dedup, persisting on save through the existing unchanged note-save path so appended codes are indistinguishable from AI-generated ones once on the note.
features.description: The provider can click any search result to append it to the Assessment section of the open note.
acceptance: Clicking a result appends the code + description to the Assessment.
The appended code persists with the note on save.
